_doc: PseudoIR v2 call-convention transform registry. DATA, not code. Sibling of ops.json. ops.json catalogs EXPRESSION operators (each sits in an expression slot, e.g. op.null_coalesce). This file catalogs CALL-CONVENTION TRANSFORMS: rewrites of how a call site's arguments map onto a callee's declared parameters. The first (and currently only) transform is xform.named_args -- keyword arguments resolved to positional at compile time. Each transform records a per-function parameter-shape record format, semantic test vectors, and per-target realization columns keyed by strategy family. Strategy and status are filled the same way as ops.json (parse-confirmed / runtime-confirmed / pending / rejected).

_strategy_ranks.native_kwargs: the target has first-class keyword/named arguments whose call semantics already match the transform's vectors; the call is emitted verbatim (no resolution at emit time). example: python make_box(width=5, label='c'). The parameter-shape record is still recorded at ingest, but a native_kwargs target does not consult it to emit.
_strategy_ranks.native_kwargs_partial: the target has no first-class keyword arguments, but a blessed language IDIOM reproduces keyword-argument call semantics exactly, so the transform emits that idiom rather than a positional call. example: typescript object-destructure -- callee declared as function f({a, b = 2}) and called f({a: 5}); key order is irrelevant and omitted keys take the destructure default, matching kwargs semantics. Recorded distinctly from native_kwargs because it is an idiom choice, not a language feature, and its precise shape (single object literal, destructure defaults on the declaration) is load-bearing.
_strategy_ranks.positional_fill: the target has NO keyword arguments and no reproducing idiom, so the transform CONSULTS the parameter-shape record and rewrites the call to a fully positional argument list in declaration order, filling omitted defaulted parameters from their default_expr. Compile-time only; no runtime cost. example: java/go make_box(5, 10, 1, 'c'). Requires the default_expr to be a pure compile-time-constant literal (see evaluate_once_caveat); an impure default is escalated, not filled.
_strategy_ranks.dart_named_required: dart HAS native named parameters, but with a declaration-site nuance: a named parameter is written inside {} in the parameter list (String f(int a, {int b = 2})) and is optional-or-required per its declaration, whereas a bare positional parameter cannot be passed by name. So the transform emits native named CALLS (f(a: 5)), but the CALLEE DECLARATION must place every transform-covered parameter inside the {} named group -- a positional-declared parameter is unreachable by name. This declaration-site {}-requirement is the recorded nuance; the call site itself is native.
_strategy_ranks.fail: the transform cannot be realized in this target with matching semantics; no lowering known. (No language is currently 'fail' for xform.named_args.)
_strategy_ranks.native_variadic: for decl.variadic (P2): the target has a first-class variadic parameter kind that auto-collects any number of call-site arguments into ONE declared parameter (a list/array/tuple), independent of any call-site spread token. example: python def f(*args) collects into a tuple; node function f(...args) into an array; java int... args, csharp params int[], ruby *args, php ...$args, swift args: Int... .
_strategy_ranks.native_variadic_coupled: for decl.variadic (P2): the declaration itself is native variadic AND is the reason the target's spread token can feed it -- the target's spread (`...`/`*`) is legal at a call site ONLY because this callee is variadic (see ops.json coupled_variadic_spread). example: go args ...int (fed by total(nums...)); kotlin vararg args: Int (fed by total(*nums)).
_strategy_ranks.native_variadic_template: for decl.variadic (P2), cpp-specific: variadic collection is realized via a compile-time parameter pack (template<class... Args>) and a fold expression, NOT a runtime container -- so the collected argument set is not introspectable as a list-typed runtime value the way other native_variadic targets are.
_strategy_ranks.no_native_variadic: for decl.variadic (P2): the target has no true variadic function mechanism; the closest substitute requires the CALLER to explicitly construct a container (e.g. total(&[1,2,3]) / total([1,2,3])), which changes call-site arity semantics from the Hub's decl.variadic (a direct N-argument call). example: rust fn total(args: &[i32]); dart int total(List<int> args). Recorded as a negative/substitute case, not a true realization.

_confirmation_status.runtime-confirmed: the lowering was executed on a real runtime in-sandbox and passed every semantic vector.
_confirmation_status.parse-confirmed: the parameter-shape record was built by parsing a real Hub def with the real tree-sitter-python grammar, and the lowering shape was emitted; runtime not exercised for this target.
_confirmation_status.pending: no runtime confirmation performed in-sandbox (no runtime/compiler available); a ready-to-run host snippet is provided in prober/pending_snippets/.
_confirmation_status.rejected: a candidate lowering was tried and FAILED (wrong shape, or a vector failed). kept as evidence, not hidden.

xforms.description: keyword-argument call sites resolved to the callee's declared parameter order at compile time, with omitted defaulted parameters filled from their recorded default expressions. Kwargs are FORBIDDEN in the Oracle Discipline matrix for Java/C++/Go; this transform is the 'COMPILE RESOLVE' the matrix itself anticipated. Ported from WFL_PseudoCoup pseudocoup/core/ledger.py param_shapes + the egress consult path (dart.py named-arg construction / _synth_init_formals). No runtime cost in any target.
xforms.signature: call f(<positional...>, <name=value...>) resolved against f's parameter-shape -> a call whose argument binding matches the callee's declaration order

param_shape_record._doc: recorded per callable at ingest (bare callee name is the key, same key space as a symbol table). Ordered list, one entry per declared parameter in declaration order.

entry_fields.name: string -- the declared parameter name; the key a keyword argument binds to.
entry_fields.position: int -- 0-based declaration index; the slot a positional argument binds to and the order positional_fill emits in.
entry_fields.has_default: bool -- whether the parameter declares a default value.
entry_fields.default_expr: string or null -- the VERBATIM source text of the default expression, or null when has_default is false. Used by positional_fill to fill an omitted argument. Its purity is judged at resolve time (see evaluate_once_caveat), NOT recorded here as a separate flag -- the text is kept faithfully so the caveat check reads the real expression.

param_shape_record.prior_art: WFL_PseudoCoup pseudocoup/core/ledger.py stores param_shapes as (name, has_default, is_trailing_lambda) tuples keyed by bare symbol name; the same bare-name-keyed, last-writer-wins ledger. Here the third tuple slot carries default_expr instead of the Kotlin-specific trailing-lambda flag, because default_expr is what positional_fill consumes. The bare-name-keyed overload-collision caveat from ledger.py's param_shapes docstring carries over: same-name functions with different signatures collide, last registration wins.

evaluate_once_caveat._doc: RECORDED CAVEAT, NOT SOLVED. A positional_fill target fills an omitted defaulted argument by pasting the callee's default_expr at the CALL SITE. For a pure compile-time-constant literal (10, "", True) this is semantics-preserving. For an IMPURE default expression (a function call like now(), another parameter's value, a mutable literal like []) it is NOT: the source language (Python) evaluates a default expression in one place only (once at def-time; the classic mutable-default-argument shared-state semantics), whereas call-site pasting evaluates it ONCE PER OMITTING CALL SITE, at call time. That changes observable behavior. The transform therefore REJECTS an impure default at resolve time rather than filling it silently.
evaluate_once_caveat.escalation: The unsolved question -- whether to instead generate an overload set at the callee (each overload supplying the default in the callee body, evaluated callee-side) or to synthesize a sentinel-and-fill-in-body scheme -- is FLAGGED for the owner, not decided. Per PLAN.md R1 escalation line: overload generation vs call-site default filling for impure defaults (evaluate-once semantics).
evaluate_once_caveat.purity_test: literal numbers, strings, and True/False/None are pure; everything else (calls, identifiers, attribute access, operators, mutable literals) is impure. Mirrors dart.py::_is_const_safe_default.
evaluate_once_caveat.resolution: DECIDED (2026-07-14): keep the ban -- only literal defaults allowed in the Hub notation. Python's def-time default evaluation is a trap not to inherit.

test_vectors.name: impure_default_rejected
test_vectors.reason: default_expr now() (and []) are impure; call-site fill would evaluate once per omitting call site -- evaluate-once escalation. Resolver raises ResolveError.

typescript.lowering: callee declared function f({a, b = <default>, ...}); call site f({a: v, ...}) -- object-destructure idiom, key order irrelevant, omitted keys take destructure default

java.lowering: resolve named->positional against param-shape, emit f(a, b, c) in declaration order with defaults filled

csharp.lowering: C# native named arguments: f(a: v, b: w); order-independent, omitted optionals take their declared default

go.lowering: resolve named->positional against param-shape, emit f(a, b, c) in declaration order with defaults filled

rust.lowering: resolve named->positional against param-shape, emit f(a, b, c) in declaration order with defaults filled (Rust has no named args and no default params)

ruby.lowering: Ruby keyword arguments: def f(a:, b: 2); f(a: 5); order-independent, omitted take declared default

php.lowering: PHP 8 named arguments: f(a: 5, b: 6); order-independent, omitted take declared default

kotlin.lowering: Kotlin named arguments: f(a = 5, b = 6); order-independent, omitted take declared default

cpp.lowering: resolve named->positional against param-shape, emit f(a, b, c) in declaration order with defaults filled (C++ has no named args; default params exist but omitted-in-the-middle is illegal, so full positional fill is required)
cpp.evidence: prober/xform_named_args/r1_results_cpp.out (g++ present in sandbox); prober/pending_snippets/named_args.cpp compiled with g++ -std=c++17 and passed 4/4 vectors

dart.lowering: Dart named parameters: declaration must place transform-covered params in the {} named group (String f(int a, {int b = 2}) or f({required int a, int b = 2})); call site f(a: 5, b: 6) is native. A positional-declared param is unreachable by name.

swift.lowering: Swift argument labels are native and MANDATORY by default: f(a: 5, b: 6); labels are part of the call and their ORDER IS FIXED to declaration -- binding is by label but reordering is not permitted. Omitted params with default values (= 2) take their default.

xforms.description: a function DECLARED to accept a variable number of arguments, COLLECTING them into one parameter (a list/array/tuple/slice per target). def f(*args) / function f(...args) / func f(xs ...int). Calling f(1,2,3) binds args=[1,2,3] inside f -- the callee's declared parameter COUNT is 1 regardless of call-site argument count. DISTINCT from op.spread_call (ops.json), which unpacks an existing sequence OUT at a call site into a callee's fixed-arity positional parameters. The two compose (spread an existing list INTO a variadic parameter) without collapsing -- proven by prober/spread_variadic/demo_spread_variadic.py vector C (spread_into_variadic). Several targets spell BOTH decl.variadic and op.spread_call with the SAME token (python *, node/php ...), disambiguated only by syntactic position: tree-sitter node type list_splat_pattern (parameter list, collect-IN) vs list_splat (call site, unpack-OUT). This is the declaration-side half of the ... three-way false friend from REPORT.md finding 4.
xforms.signature: def f(*params) / function f(...params) -- declare a trailing parameter that collects any number of call-site arguments into one list/array/tuple/slice-typed parameter

param_shape_record._doc: recorded per callable at ingest: whether the callee has a trailing variadic-collecting parameter, and what container shape the target realizes it as.

entry_fields.name: string -- the declared variadic parameter's name (binds the collected container inside the callee body).
entry_fields.collects_into: string -- the target-specific container type the collected arguments bind as (python tuple; node/ruby/php/java/csharp array; go slice; kotlin IntArray; cpp parameter pack; rust/dart N/A).
entry_fields.coupled_to_call_site_spread: bool -- whether this target's spread token (`*`/`...`) is legal at a call site ONLY when the callee's trailing parameter is ALSO declared variadic. true for go, kotlin; false for python/node/ruby/php (spread and variadic are independently spellable).

example_for_total.name: args
example_for_total.collects_into: tuple (python) / array (node, ruby, php, java, csharp) / slice (go) / IntArray (kotlin) / parameter pack (cpp) / [Int] (swift) / N/A (rust, dart)

test_vectors.name: variadic_collect
test_vectors.note: callee's param COUNT is 1 regardless of call-site argument count.

test_vectors.name: spread_into_variadic
test_vectors.note: sharpest contrast -- touches BOTH op.spread_call and decl.variadic in one call, proving they compose without collapsing.

cpp.lowering: template<class... Args> int total(Args... args) { return (args + ... + 0); } -- collects into a compile-time parameter pack, C++17 fold expression

dart.lowering: NO native variadic parameter kind. Idiomatic replacement: int total(List<int> args) => args.fold(0,(a,b)=>a+b) -- caller must build the list (total([1,2,3])). This target's `...` token means collection-literal spread only, categorically unrelated to decl.variadic -- the family's false friend.
dart.evidence: p2_results/spread_dart.out 2026-07-14 host run -- confirms the List<int>-param SUBSTITUTE passes vector B; still not a true native variadic (strategy stays no_native_variadic)

swift.lowering: func total(_ args: Int...) -> Int { args.reduce(0, +) } -- args collects into an [Int] array. Native for direct N-argument calls (total(1,2,3)), but Swift has NO array-to-variadic spread, so spread_into_variadic (vector C) has no realization here -- only variadic_collect (vector B) is native.
